newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan gasoline retail price unchanged - survey.
newsitem.headline: Japan gasoline retail price unchanged - survey.

text.p: The average price of gasoline at petrol stations throughout Japan was 106 yen per litre as of February 10, unchanged from a month earlier, a research centre said on Tuesday.

The retail price was cheapest in Ibaraki prefecture, north of Tokyo, at 99 yen and most expensive in Tottori prefecture, southern Japan, at 117 yen, according to a survey by the Oil Information Service Centre.
Tax accounts for more than half of the retail price.
National average gasoline retail prices have been steady for the last two months, after rising in December for the first time since October 1992.
Refiners have recently been raising their wholesale oil product prices in line with firmer crude prices and the weaker yen against the dollar.
However, retail prices of gasoline and gas oil have been weak, pressured by a price war among petrol stations.
The average retail price of gas oil as of February 10 was also unchanged from the previous month, at 83 yen per litre, the survey showed.
The retail price of kerosene, used for heating, was 903 yen per 18 litres, up four yen from a month earlier.
